source.author: lucan
source.text: Tot potuere manus adiungere Seston Abydo, Ingestoque solo Phryxeum elidere pontum, Aut Pelopis latis Ephyren abrumpere regnis, Et ratibus longae flexus donare Maleae, Aut aliquem mundi, quamvis natura negasset, In melius mutare locum.
source.text_original: Tot potuere manus adiungere Seston Abydo, / Ingestoque solo Phryxeum elidere pontum, / Aut Pelopis latis Ephyren abrumpere regnis, / Et ratibus longae flexus donare Maleae, / Aut aliquem mundi, quamvis natura negasset, / In melius mutare locum.
source.text_english: Hands were able to join Sestos to Abydos, to level the Phrixean sea by piling up earth, to tear Ephyre away from the broad kingdom of Pelops, and to give to ships the bends of Malea’s long coast, or to transform some place of the world into something better, though nature had denied it.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: septem Aurora vias totidemque peregerat umbras Luna polo, dirimique procul non aequore visa coeperat a gemina discedere Sestos Abydo.
reuse.text_original: septem Aurora vias totidemque peregerat umbras / Luna polo, dirimique procul non aequore visa / coeperat a gemina discedere Sestos Abydo.
reuse.text_english: Aurora had completed seven courses, and the Moon had likewise completed seven shades in the sky, and Sestos, seen from far off, had begun to be separated from Abydos by the twin sea, now appearing to draw apart.
